title: Sorrel weed (Ubwunyu bwa Nyamanza) in Banana

Header: Sorrel weed (Ubwunyu bwa Nyamanza) in Banana
Oxalis latifolia Ubwunyu bwa Nyamanza (Kinyarwanda); Oseille, trèfle (French); Sorrel (English)

Prevention: Practice intercropping of beans-banana alternated with mulching as this does not allow
Oxalis latifolia to thrive and spread
Temeda, Tripsacum, Pennisetum spp. or dry banana leaves (15-20 cm thick)
Defoliation by mowing has to be repeated many times as weed emerges to have substantial effect
O. latifolia bulb with small daughter bulbs (bulbils) © John
Monitoring: Look for small plants with 14-15 leaves.
Each leaf is composed of 3 fishtail shaped leaflets linked to one other.Their bulbs look like small whitish carrots (diameter: 1-2 cm).
When seeds are formed, they are orange to dark yellow, about 1 mm long and ribbed
Check for the presence of the weed 2 weeks after mulching
Direct Control (Non-chemical): A combination of deep tillage and exposure of bulbs to desiccate can be helpful

Oxalis latifolia in such a way that bulbs do not remain in soil; this is easiest to achieve in mulched plantations as the soil is soft and humid; burry the residues in a pit to avoid bulb re-sprouting within the field
Puccinia oxalidis is a biological control agent; consult extension agency (Rwanda
Board) for its use to control
